CPI.name: Consumer Price Index
CPI.desc: Inflation as felt by US consumers — the flagship gauge the Fed leans on for rate decisions.
CPI.high: Hotter-than-expected inflation → rate cuts pushed back → typically bearish for stocks & crypto
CPI.low: Cooling inflation → stronger rate-cut hopes → typically bullish

PCE.name: PCE Price Index
PCE.desc: The Fed's officially preferred inflation gauge — same family as CPI.
PCE.high: Persistent price pressure → tightening fears → typically bearish
PCE.low: Cooling prices → rate-cut hopes → typically bullish

PPI.name: Producer Price Index
PPI.desc: Wholesale prices received by businesses — read as a leading indicator for CPI.
PPI.high: Rising producer prices → reflation fears → typically bearish

FOMC.name: Fed Rate Decision
FOMC.desc: The Federal Reserve's benchmark rate decision — the single biggest event for global asset markets.
FOMC.high: Higher-than-expected rate (hawkish) → tighter liquidity → typically bearish
FOMC.low: Lower rate / cut (dovish) → more liquidity → typically bullish
FOMC.note: When in line with expectations, the statement and dot plot (future path) move markets more than the rate itself.

NFP.name: Nonfarm Payrolls
NFP.desc: Jobs added in the US over a month — the flagship gauge of economic strength.
NFP.high: Strong hiring → solid economy → typically bullish
NFP.low: Slowing hiring → recession fears → typically bearish
NFP.note: Too-strong numbers can flip the reaction on 'delayed rate cut' fears.

GDP.name: Gross Domestic Product
GDP.desc: Growth of the entire US economy — the overall report card of the cycle.
GDP.high: Solid growth → earnings hopes → typically bullish
GDP.low: Slowing growth → recession fears → typically bearish
GDP.note: An overheated surprise can also be read as rate pressure.

RETAIL.name: Retail Sales
RETAIL.desc: US consumer spending — a direct read on consumption, ~70% of the US economy.
RETAIL.high: Solid spending → healthy economy → typically bullish
RETAIL.low: Weak spending → slowdown fears → typically bearish
RETAIL.note: In inflationary phases, hot spending can be read the other way as rate pressure.

ISM.name: ISM Manufacturing Index
ISM.desc: Manufacturing purchasing managers' sentiment. Above 50 = expansion, below = contraction.
ISM.high: Manufacturing expansion → healthy economy → typically bullish

UNEMP.name: Unemployment Rate
UNEMP.desc: The share of people without jobs. Lower means a stronger labor market.
UNEMP.high: Rising unemployment → slowdown fears → typically bearish
UNEMP.low: Solid employment → healthy economy → typically bullish

CLAIMS.name: Initial Jobless Claims
CLAIMS.desc: People newly filing for unemployment benefits in a week — the labor market's weekly bulletin.
CLAIMS.high: Rising claims → labor weakening → typically bearish
CLAIMS.low: Falling claims → solid employment → typically bullish

OTHER.name: Economic Indicator
OTHER.desc: A key US economic indicator. The surprise vs forecast is what moves markets.
OTHER.high: Above forecast → healthy-economy signal → typically bullish
OTHER.low: Below forecast → slowdown signal → typically bearish

archive.title: Validation Archive
archive.subtitle: What we tested and why it passed or failed — a rejection is not a failure, it is knowledge that an idea has no edge. All figures are measured.

h1.title: H1 — Fibonacci retracement 'confirmed entry'
h1.concl: The idea: waiting for a close back above the level after a touch should be safer than entering immediately. Out-of-sample, both win rate and profit factor got worse than immediate entry — the cost of waiting for confirmation exceeded its benefit. Rejected.
h1.stat: 354 reclaim trades (IS+OOS) · OOS PF 0.94 vs immediate 1.12 (1h) · difference p≈0.69

h2.title: H2 — Volume filter on breakout candles
h2.concl: We tested whether keeping only breakouts with unusually high volume (z≥2) filters out fake breakouts. As a filter it passed — the trades it removed really were worse — but the strategy itself lost money out-of-sample, so instead of production it goes to a 4-hour shadow.
h2.stat: 3,688 filter-ON trades · OOS 4h PF 0.79 vs 0.66 unfiltered · suppressed group 0.57

h3.title: H3 — Break, then retest entry at S/R zones
h3.concl: The textbook pattern: break resistance, wait for the pullback to confirm support, then enter. Measured, it was no better than entering immediately — and both lost. Even textbook patterns get rejected by data.
h3.stat: 416 retest trades · OOS PF 0.52 vs immediate 0.54 · avg return −1.02%

h4.title: H4 — Volatility squeeze breakout
h4.concl: The idea: ride whichever direction breaks out after the bands compress. It contributed an improvement over baseline, but profit factor never crossed 1 and fees made it worse. Rejected.
h4.stat: 1,795 squeeze entries · OOS PF 0.59 vs baseline 0.55 · 0.49 after fees · 34 max consecutive losses

h5.title: H5 — KST hour-of-day / weekday seasonality
h5.concl: We statistically tested five folk claims like '9am is strong' and 'Wednesdays go up'. All five failed significance — even the closest one, the Wednesday effect, missed the multiple-testing threshold (p<0.01).
h5.stat: 0 of 5 claims supported · lowest primary-test p 0.045 (threshold 0.01) · BTC·ETH + 6 cross-validation symbols

candle.title: Candlestick pattern calibration
candle.concl: We scored 9 patterns × 3 timeframes = 27 combinations on measured data; only 3 survived (1h bullish engulfing, 4h piercing, 1d three white soldiers). The other 24 score zero — famous patterns get no credit without an edge.
candle.stat: 3 of 27 adopted · 1h bullish engulfing OOS n=225 +67bps (t 1.61) · 4h piercing OOS n=155 +71bps

timing.title: Entry engine v2 — confluence factor validation
timing.concl: In the first validation pass (2026-07), only 9 of 42 entry-factor candidates (factor × timeframe × direction) survived — all long at the time; showing unvalidated shorts would be dishonest. Deep-history revalidation (v4) then produced our first validated short factor (4h OBV divergence) and the holdout eliminated 2 more, so today 11 combinations (including 1 short) participate in firing.
timing.stat: First pass: 9 of 42 survived (all long) → 11 firing today after deep-history & holdout revalidation (1 short) · deep history: 860k 1h bars (incl. 2021–22 bear market) · holdout: 6 unseen symbols, 220k bars

sr.title: S/R levels — volume bonus
sr.concl: Adversarial validation of the rule that gives extra weight to high-volume levels showed one-off volume spikes distorting the bonus. So we narrowed it to multi-touch (2+) structural levels only — narrowing scope is also a validation outcome.
sr.stat: Qualitative (adversarial) validation — outside the statistical gate · bonus restricted to 2+ touch levels
